summary: The repair was applied only to the independent patched copy: resolve the configured root and joined target immediately after the join and before the extensionless append, reject unless the target equals the root or begins with the root plus the path separator, and reuse the existing 404 page. A 15-case suite on the patched copy passed all cases: three ordinary in-root requests returned 200 with bodies whose hashes matched the source files, seven traversal shapes returned 404 with no marker bytes, encoded shapes remained 404 for behavioral parity, and missing and extensionless-no-index cases stayed 404. The same suite against the vulnerable copy passed 8 of 15 and failed exactly the seven traversal cases with marker bytes present, so the suite discriminates. Sibling-suffix, boundary-equality, and placement-before-append probes were all confirmed; symlink containment remained untested.
next_hint: The repaired handler passed a discriminating 15-case suite and the vulnerable copy failed exactly the traversal cases. Close the remaining questions: query strings, a relative root under a changed working directory, a sibling directory sharing a long name prefix, concurrent requests, and the measured behavior of a symlink inside the root; then package the repair as a unified diff and a machine-readable patch record.
